First listed 2026-02-23 · episode or wrap

George Noble on Gold’s Rise, Crypto Doubts & Tesla’s Struggles | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 47

George Noble favors energy, metals and foreign-market rotation while opposing technology, Bitcoin, Tesla and Opendoor. Eisman challenges the timing of dollar-collapse arguments, discloses a Strategy short, and explicitly withholds endorsement of the broad sector call. Their strongest shared analysis concerns gross-versus-net revenue comparisons and the path risks of shorting. Primary filings support Tesla earnings deterioration but challenge the claimed consecutive consolidated revenue declines and show positive nine-month cash generation. The ten-year yield exceeded 5% during 2026, while full-year calls remain open.

YouTube · 2026-02-23 ↗Substack · 2026-02-23 ↗
Useful analyst-quality signals are the explicit discussion of failed timing, refusal to equate a poor business with an immediately profitable short, and scrutiny of misleading revenue comparisons. Weaknesses include using price action as proof of fundamentals, broad social-substitution explanations without flow evidence, and speculative valuation analogies. Several guest forecasts have explicit calendar-year horizons that remain open at the cutoff. The host’s Strategy short is distinct from his explicit refusal to short Tesla.

YouTube automatic captions; speaker attribution requires context

George Noble is the buy-side guest. Steve Eisman’s challenges, specific endorsements, Strategy disclosure and closing reservations are separately attributed. The closing recap is essential to avoid treating the whole guest portfolio as Eisman’s.

  • Opendoor illustrative house prices are garbled in captions; the economic gross-versus-net distinction is preserved without silently repairing dollar figures.
  • Noble’s sector call is not Eisman’s: the host explicitly says in the closing recap that he remains unconvinced.
  • The Treasury-below-4.5% scenario is a hypothetical used to discuss rotation, not Noble’s forecast.
  • Tesla total revenue, automotive revenue, GAAP EPS and adjusted EPS are different measures; the interview shifts between them.
  • Personal fund returns, prior short calls and allegations about promoters are not independently verified performance records.

How he reasons here

  • Require a why-now catalyst rather than repeat a longstanding macro vulnerability.
  • Separate a company’s economics, valuation and the timing constraints of a short position.
  • Normalize gross-versus-net revenue and inventory exposure before comparing valuation multiples.
  • Treat market-price confirmation as feedback, not independent proof of a causal thesis.
  • Reserve-currency network effects can resist displacement without guaranteeing unchanged purchasing power.
